Here's an interesting population of S. montana from greenville Co, SC that I know very little about...other than the fact that these plants are starting to look pretty amazing! The shape on some of these are much longer than other genotypes I've grown in the past. I will know more about this population as the plants mature: for now, they're just tiny plantlets. And yes, I'm doing my best to propagate these: due to the relentless pressure I've been getting from multiple people, I divided tiny plants unsucessfully earlier this year which set me back a little bit, but there still should be a few available in the near future. What you're looking at are literally the biggest plants that I have of this population. Photos taken 8/7/18:






Looking forward to seeing what this one looks like as it matures:

posts.body_html:
Received one of these cool little dudes from Mike last year, December 2019. It's by far my favorite purp in the collection, and boy is it vigorous!

Here it is in March, before it broke dormancy in May (Late start this year in New York! Unsure if spring will earlier next season.):


And here's the same plant now, photo taken today, 10/23/2020:



My yard only gets at most 8 hours of sun during the peak of the summer, so this one hasn't colored up to its full potential. That's not too bad though because the lime green almost glows!

posts.body_html: So far I've bought three S. montana (South Carolina population) seedlings from Barry Rice.  Unfortunately I killed the first one cause I didn't protect it while it transitioned from California weather to Washington weather.  The second I got last year and is doing well.  I just bought a third, and while I know the appearance will change as it matures I'm currently smitten with it.  It's sooooo gorgeous!

posts.body_html:
I have one S. purpurea var. montana Greenville Co., SC that I grew out from a randomly-selected seedling.

July 2019


July 2020 - check out that growth spurt!


Sweet interior venation - the finer veins are obliterated by the bold major ones which I've also noticed in Mike's pictures. Rorschach anyone?


June 2021 - wait, another growth spurt? Yup!


September 2021 - So I was thinking that September is peak montana season since that seems to be when the greatest range of color is expressed in most of my montanas [side note: I think those plantlets are probably from stolons, they're well off the base where the rhizome should be! Very cool.]

but there's just something about the purples after going through dormancy that's unreal!
March 2022
